idle.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / identity-preserve. Edit target Image1, an EXISTING GAME ANIMATION SPRITE SHEET. This is a COLOR-ONLY edit of finished art. Retain EVERY existing pose exactly, the exact hair silhouette and hair tufts, face shapes, eyes, anatomy, frame count, alignment, outline weight, clothing and proportions. Do not invent a character or redraw an animation.
Change red-brown hair to BLACK HAIR painted directly into the sprite pixels. Use neutral near-black shadows with subtle charcoal highlights that follow the existing hair shading. Remove all red/brown hair, including small tufts and fringe. Keep eyes/skin/face completely distinct from hair, with clean boundaries. No algorithmic cutoff or horizontal color bands.
SKIN REFERENCE: Image2 (when present) is the original idle sprite sheet and is authoritative for skin. Keep that ORIGINAL darker warm skin tone and its shaded ramp exactly, including face, ears, neck and bare hands. The action face and hands must match the original idle/walk skin color. Do NOT lighten, bleach, turn yellow, oversaturate or add peach/orange glow. In idle and walk edits, preserve the existing skin colors unchanged. Preserve cream cuffs as cream, olive shirt, ochre yellow scarf, brown belt trousers and boots exactly. Same light/shadow hue and tone in every frame.
LAYOUT: Keep a regular grid EXACTLY 4 columns and FIVE rows, same arrangement and cell order as target. Keep individual sprite positions and all transparent margins, no trimming, no rearranging, no new movement. Rows remain pure right profile, front-right, front, back-right, back. Make all sprites complete, no cropped tufts, no detached pixels, no trails, no extra limbs. Transparent alpha background, not a checkerboard or colored backdrop. No text, no labels, no grid lines. Keep the target sheet's aspect ratio and dimensions as closely as possible. Finished game sprite art, not a concept sheet.
EDIT TARGET ACTION: idle. Preserve all 4 existing frames per row.
